title.label: Good app, extremely laggy on iPhone

content.label:
Been using Notion for years, I love the app, and though it takes some time to understand how it all works once you do it’s simple and fun to utilize. 

With that said the app is really really laggy on iPhone. 

A few issues I’ve found using Notion on iPhone:  

1. I cannot delete text on the app. Say I select text and press the x button to delete it on my iPhone keyboard, it will not delete. Even if I press x to delete it without selecting the text it won’t delete so I have to select and press the ‘cut’ selection.

2. Certain pages won’t load when I try to open them, it’ll display the loading icon for awhile and then seemingly crash and close the app.

3. Inserting photos and the page auto-scrolls downwards to the end of the page. Pretty self explanatory, but when I insert photos and then try to move them around the page it’ll start auto scrolling to the bottom of the page. 

4. The app freezing. Sometimes it just freezes and I have to close the app and reopen it. 

5. Accidentally selecting an item (like a divider) and the app won’t let me close the menu that pops up after where the ‘insert below’ option shows up. 


These are just a few issues I’ve found while using the app on iPhone. I truly do love the app, I just don’t like that these issues are so frequent. 

(side note: i have deleted and reinstalled the app in the hopes of fixing these glitches, but it doesn’t fix them.)

I love Notion, I love the various templates I can use and how more organized I feel once I started using Notion—the only problem being… how buggy it is: widgets on phone screen don’t work properly; they just keep loading endlessly…Sometimes you can’t delete text; it just stays there. You have to select the text and do the cut option just to get rid of it, which is annoying. Sometimes the screen just freezes; have no clue why. I think this app is great. I love Notion, like seriously… it's a game changer, but I feel like I'd love this app much more if it just... wasn't so buggy and sometimes impossible to work with.

title.label: Great before the most recent update (2026)

content.label: Users used to be able to browse and add templates from the web app, desktop app, or the mobile app. Recently, they removed that ability for users on the mobile app. Incredibly annoying to have to log in on a PC just to add a template. The whole point of Notion is to increase productivity. Forcing users to jump through hoops to use basic functions of the app only prevents productivity.

For example, when I create a database and add multi-select options, trying to hold down on one of the options to move it (I sometimes switch the options to be in a certain order) causes the page to spazz out of control and start auto-scrolling back to the top and it doesn’t stop unless I tap out of the page and reenter. I can’t help but feel like the effort put into maintaining the user experience in the desktop version, whilst adding in new features, isn’t being applied to the app version, which is very disappointing. title.label: The latest update renders the app useless

content.label:
I use the app version of Notion primarily for sending and using links within tables and databases while I’m away from my computer - recipes, articles, ideas, etc.

The latest update truncates the content of the tables and databases to 5 characters, so I can only figure out what I’m accessing only when I’m on my desktop or mobile versions of Notion.

Hate it. Frustrating AF. Please fix it (by untruncating) so I can continue using the app within my daily workflows. 

Also hate the update that randomly starts consuming AI agent coins, but that’s mostly a business model thing rather than a serious usability issue.

This app reminds me of those knockoff AI-built apps that try to reinvent everything but end up being overly complicated and difficult to use. What should be a simple daily planning and logging system quickly turned into what felt like an IT database management project.

I used it for one day, and before I could even get a simple planner set up in a way that made sense, I had already run out of credits/tokens. It seems like the app is trying to reinvent the wheel with every little feature, adding unnecessary complexity instead of making things easier.

Honestly, it’s just too much for me. I’ll stick to journaling on paper—it’s simpler, faster, and actually works.
